transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having some trouble with eating lately. 

It's mostly at night. After everyone goes to bed, I'll tell myself I'm just having a bite of leftovers. But then... I don't know. I realize I've eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, and... dessert from a client dinner, and just whatever snacks are in the pantry. All in one sitting. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you've eaten?
No... I don't do any of that. I just... no.
Do you feel fully awake and aware when you're eating at night, or does it feel more like you're on autopilot, like you're not completely in control of what you're doing?

I'm awake. But... yeah, I guess it is kind of like autopilot. 

Once I start... especially if things were tense with my husband earlier... it just feels like the decision-making part of me goes offline. I'll actually be thinking to myself, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough.' But I just... I keep reaching for more anyway.
Do these nighttime eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

I mean... I'm still working. I can still do my job. But... yeah, it bothers me. 

The mornings after, I just... I feel really drained. And embarrassed. I've actually started canceling on people. Like, skipping yoga, or... just things I used to do. I just don't really want to be around anyone when I feel like that.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen? Are they happening most nights, or only occasionally?
It's... well, for the last three months or so, it's been at least one night almost every week. Usually after an argument, or if I had to work late. Some weeks it's... it's twice.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you're unable to control how much you're eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?
Yeah... like I mentioned earlier, it's exactly that. Even when I know I've had enough, and I'm practically telling myself to stop... I just can't seem to make myself do it.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you can't stop eating once you start, even if you want to?

I... yes, I think I already said that. It's... it's like the decision-making part of me just goes offline. Once I start, especially if it's been a tense night... with my husband... I just keep reaching for more. Even when I'm thinking, 'Patricia, stop, this is enough,' I just... I can't.
When you have these nighttime eating episodes, would you say you're eating a definitely larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances?

I suppose so. It's... well, I'll tell myself I'm just going to have some leftovers after everyone goes to bed. But then... I don't know, I'll realize I've eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, plus whatever dessert was left from a client dinner, and... just whatever snacks I find in the pantry. All at once. So... yes, it's a lot.

Do these nighttime eating episodes happen after you've already gone to bed and fallen asleep, like you wake up and find yourself eating, or are you still awake and decide to eat while you're still up?
No... I'm still awake. I don't... I don't wake up from sleep to do it or anything like that. It's just while I'm still up.
Have you noticed that these nighttime eating episodes happen more often when you're feeling down, depressed, or have lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
No... I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel... depressed. I still go to work and do what I need to do. So... no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you usually feel like eating breakfast in the morning, or do you often skip it because you don’t feel hungry?
Um... no, I usually eat breakfast. I don't really skip it.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than you normally would?

Um... yeah, I suppose I do. I'll just be standing at the kitchen island, or... maybe scrolling through some work emails, and I eat so fast I barely even taste it. Sometimes I just look down and... the containers are empty before I've really registered what I was eating.
Do you feel like you have absolutely no control over your eating once these episodes start, and does that lack of control happen every time?

Um... I suppose... yes. It’s... well, once I start, especially if it’s been a tense night... with my husband... it just feels like the decision-making part of me goes offline. I’ll actually be thinking to myself, ‘Patricia, stop, this is enough,’ but... I just keep reaching for more anyway. So... yeah, I guess I do.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you have absolutely no control over how much you're eating, and that this loss of control happens every single time?

Um... yes. Like I was just saying... it's pretty much every time. Once I start... especially after those tense evenings with my husband... I just can't seem to stop. Even when I'm literally telling myself that it's enough, it doesn't matter. I just keep reaching for more anyway. So, yes... it's every time.
Do these nighttime eating episodes usually happen after you've been feeling a specific emotional state, like stress, sadness, or anger?
Um... I guess so. I'm not really sure if it's always one specific thing. It's just... usually after a long day, I suppose.
